analytic.title: A Hybrid Scheduling Scheme for Hard, Soft and Non-Real-time Tasks*

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: This paper proposes a hybrid scheduling scheme for hard, soft and non-real-time tasks. The scheme creates a constant utilization server for each real-time scheduling policy and a total bandwidth server for all the non-real-time tasks with time sharing scheduling policy. Each server has a scheduler, called server scheduler, which is responsible for executing the ready-to-run tasks with the same scheduling policy as the server. All the servers are scheduled by the bottom operating system scheduler according to EDF algorithm.

The schedulability test is also presented in this paper. The hybrid scheme can be used to implement different real time systems with different goals (such as hard, soft or hybrid real-time systems) and can provide the real-time services with different QoS to the different task modes by adjusting every constant utilization server's size. This scheme also simplifies the schedulability analysis and validates the schedulability of the tasks with one scheduling policy independently of the tasks with other scheduling policies. The experimental results show that the hybrid scheme is an efficient scheduling scheme .

div.head: Introduction
div.p: The traditional real time scheduling methods, which are dedicated to some special applications, are not suitable for these systems any more. To cater for the requirements of open real-time systems, the open realtime scheduler must be able to process hard, soft and non-real-time tasks jointly and separate scheduling mechanism from scheduling policy [1]. The mechanism is in the kernel but the policy is set by a user process. It can permit the user to choose the desirable scheduling policy for each application at their wills, even for each task in his application. Therefore, multiple real-time scheduling policies are permitted to coexist in the open real-time system.

RTAI [2] is an open source project about real-time Linux, which permits EDF and RM to coexist in the system. In RTAI, the priorities of the tasks executed on EDF basis are higher than the priority of any task scheduled according to other scheduling policies. Its main shortcoming is that if the real-time tasks on EDF basis occupy too much CPU utilization, the deadlines of real-time tasks with other scheduling policies can not be met well.

A general real-time scheduling framework is presented in [3]. In the framework, priority-driven (PD), share-driven (SD) and time-driven (TD) paradigms are integrated together. But this is only simple accumulation. Only one paradigm can be adopted when the system runs. The framework does not separate scheduling mechanism from scheduling policy. The users can not choose a desirable scheduling policy for their applications at their wills. Thus this scheduling framework only meets the requirements of a kind of users at one time and is not suitable for scheduling hard, soft and non-real-time tasks jointly.

In [4,5], a two-level hierarchical scheme for open real-time systems is proposed. In this scheme, when the operating system admits a new real-time application into the system, a dedicated constant utilization server is created to execute the application. At the top level, the operating system allocates processor time to the servers, sets their deadlines, and schedules the servers according to EDF algorithm. At the low level, the scheduler of the server for each application schedules the tasks within the application according to a prioritydriven algorithm (such as EDF, RM) chosen for the application.

In [6], the open system architecture follows the one developed by [4,5] and replaces the underlying OS scheduler with a fixed-priority scheduler, such as RM scheduler. Multiple scheduling policies are permitted to coexist in the systems with the two-level hierarchical schemes [4][5][6]. In these schemes, a server is a special task. Each application needs a dedicated server. But if many real-time applications coexist in the system, the servers will take too much CPU and memory. The scheduling latency will also be very high. The tasks in a parallel and/or distributed application should be executed concurrently. In these schemes [4][5][6], an application is executed by a dedicated server, so the tasks of an application can only be allocated to one processor even in parallel and/or distributed systems and can not be executed concurrently. Thus, the twolevel hierarchical schemes [4][5][6] can not meet the requirements of the real-time applications with parallel threads/processes in parallel and/or distributed realtime systems.

In [7], the two-level hierarchical scheme is extended into parallel and distributed systems. However, the extension is based on the assumptions that no process migration is allowed and no parallel threads can be executed by a process, so it only can improve the concurrency between the applications but not improve the concurrency between the tasks within one parallel application. Additionally, some complex real-time applications may consist of real-time part and non-realtime part. For example, a real-time information processing application can be divided into real-time and non-real-time parts. Real-time part is responsible for processing data, and the data is displayed by the non-real-time part. The two parts in these real-time applications should be scheduled by real-time and nonreal-time scheduling policies respectively. But an application is scheduled by only one policy in the twolevel hierarchical schemes. This is not reasonable.

In this paper, we propose a hybrid scheduling scheme for hard, soft and non-real-time tasks, which is based on but extends the two-level hierarchical architecture in [4,5]. The rest of the paper is structured as follows: section 2 presents the architecture of hybrid scheduling scheme. Schedulability condition of realtime task is discussed in section 3. In section 4, we evaluate the hybrid scheduling scheme. Finally, in section 5, some concluding remarks are made.

div.head: Architecture of Hybrid Scheduling Scheme
div.p: According to the two-level hierarchical architecture [4,5], every real-time application is executed by a dedicated constant utilization server according to one scheduling policy. In our hybrid scheduling scheme, (1) we take all the tasks with EDF algorithm as an application A EDF , all the tasks with RM algorithm as an application A RM , all the tasks with SD algorithm as an application A SD ; (2) the applications A EDF , A RM and A SD are executed by constant utilization server CUS EDF , CUS RM and CUS SD , respectively; (3) we set the size of CUS EDF to a constant (0≤ ≤1), the size of CUS RM to a constant (0≤ ≤1), and the size of CUS SD to a constant (0≤ ≤1), in addition, the total size of all the servers is less than or equal to one; (4) all the non-real-time tasks are executed by a total bandwidth server [8]; (5) at the bottom level, all the servers are scheduled by the OS scheduler on EDF basis.

Under the conditions of (1), (2), (3), (4), and (5), the maintenance algorithm of servers in [4,5] can be used in our hybrid scheme directly. The difference between our hybrid scheme and the two-level hierarchical architecture [4,5] is that the schedulability analysis of the tasks with one scheduling policy is independent of the tasks with another scheduling policy in the former, but the schedulability analysis of an application is independent of the other applications in the latter.

Additionally, through this extension, our hybrid scheduling scheme is not only suitable for the application with both real-time part and non-real-time part, but also suitable for the application with parallel threads/processes in parallel and/or distributed realtime systems because the tasks in an application can be executed by different servers in our scheme. Moreover, the hybrid scheme can be used to implement different real time systems with different goals (such as hard, soft or hybrid real-time systems) and can provide the real-time services with different QoS to the different task modes by adjusting every constant utilization server's size. The architecture of the hybrid scheduling scheme for hard, soft and non-real-time tasks is shown in Fig. 1.

div.head: Scheduling Hierarchy
div.p: The applications are scheduled and executed according to the two-level hierarchical scheme shown in Fig. 1. At the bottom level, the scheduler provided by the operating system, called OS scheduler, maintains all the servers (refer [4,5] for the detailed maintenance algorithm of servers). The OS scheduler schedules all the servers in the system according to EDF algorithm.

As shown in Fig. 1, when the OS scheduler selects a server to execute, the server executes the task at the head of its ready queue. The server S p for scheduling algorithm p in the system also has a scheduler, called server scheduler, namely top-level scheduler. The server scheduler of S p schedules ready-to-run tasks and places them in the ready queue of S p according to scheduling algorithm p. In contrast, the operating system schedules all the non-real-time tasks, which runs in a slower time-sharing environment.

div.head: Operations of the OS Scheduler
div.p: Fig. 2 shows the operations of the OS scheduler. When the system starts, the operating system creates the total bandwidth server TBS TS to schedule all nonreal-time tasks according to a time-sharing algorithm, the constant utilization server [4,5] CUS SD with size to execute soft real-time tasks according to a SD algorithm based on General Processor Sharing (GPS) [9][10][11][12] and the constant utilization server CUS p for hard real-time scheduling algorithm p (such as CUS EDF with size for EDF, CUS RM with size for RM).

The OS scheduler always admits non-real-time applications, but it admits a real-time application into the system only when all the real-time tasks in the application meet the schedulability condition described in Section 3. When the OS scheduler admits a new real-time application A k , each task in A k is allocated to the corresponding server with the same scheduling algorithm as the task. The server scheduler then inserts the task in the proper location in the server's ready queue. The time taken for inserting the newly released task into the ready queue is either negligibly small compared with the execution times of all the tasks in the system or is accounted for by including the server scheduler as a system task. When the system exits, the operating system destroys all the servers. We assume that the total server size of all the constant utilization servers and total bandwidth servers in the system is less than or equal to one at all times.

div.head: Initiation:
div.p: Create a server for each scheduling policy in the system, such as a total bandwidth server TBS TS with size U 0 for non-real-time tasks, a constant utilization server CUS SD with size U SD = for soft real-time tasks, a constant utilization server CUS EDF with size U EDF = for hard real-time tasks with EDF algorithm, a constant utilization server CUS RM with size U RM = for hard realtime tasks with RM algorithm. Set current processor utilization U of each server to zero.

div.head: Acceptance test and admission of real-time application A k :
div.p: If all the real-time tasks in A k are schedulable, accept A k , or reject A k .

div.head: Maintenance of each server S p :
div.p: Replenish the budget and set the deadline of server S p depending on the characteristics of S p according to the maintenance algorithm of the constant utilization server in [4,5] and the maintenance algorithm of the total bandwidth server in [8].

div.head: Interaction with server scheduler of each server S p :
div.p: When a task i with execution time e i and relative deadline d i is released, invoke the server scheduler of S p (with the same scheduling algorithm p as the task i ) to insert i in S p 's ready queue and set the current total utilization U of the server S p to U + e i / d i .

div.head: Scheduling of all servers:
div.p: Schedule all servers on the EDF basis.

div.head: Constant Utilization Server
div.p: Constant utilization server [4,5] is defined by its server size, which is the fractional processor utilization allocated to the server. Each constant utilization server becomes eligible for execution when the operating system gives it some (>0) execution budget. The budget is consumed (i.e., decreased by one unit per unit of time) whenever the server executes. The server is no longer eligible for execution when its budget is exhausted (i.e., the budget becomes zero). It becomes eligible for execution again when the operating system replenishes its budget (i.e., sets its budget to some positive value again).
In preemptive systems, the operating system replenishes the server budget and sets the server deadline of a constant utilization server with constant size U according to the following statements:

1. Initially, the budget of the server is zero, and the deadline d is also zero; 2. When a task i with execution time e i and relative deadline d i arrives (i.e., is released and placed in the ready queue of the server) at time r i while the ready queue is empty, if d ≤ r i , set the server budget to b and deadline d to r i + b/U; 3. At the deadline d of the server, if a task i with execution time e i is waiting at the head of the ready queue, set the budget to b and move the deadline to d + b/U. In these rules, b is equal to the remaining execution time of the task i at the head of the ready queue of the constant utilization server.

div.head: Total Bandwidth Server
div.p: When the k-th aperiodic soft request arrives at time t = r k , it receives a deadline
div.formula: d k = max(r k , d k-1 )+ s k U C
div.p: where C k is the execution time of the request and U s is the server utilization factor (i.e., its bandwidth).

According to the total bandwidth server algorithm [8], the server budget is replenished immediately after the budget becomes zero if the ready queue of the server is not empty. According to the constant utilization server algorithm, the budget is replenished no earlier than the current server deadline. Consequently, a constant utilization server cannot make use of any background time, while a total bandwidth server can. In our scheduling scheme, we use constant utilization server to execute hard real-time tasks, which can save some background time. We use total bandwidth server to execute soft real-time tasks, which can make good use of background time. So our scheme can not only guarantee the deadlines of hard real-time tasks but also improve the responsiveness of the soft real-time tasks.

div.head: Schedulability Condition of Real-time Task
div.p: The system always admits non-real-time applications, but it admits a real-time application into the system only when all the real-time tasks in the application meet the schedulability condition. If all the real-time tasks in a real-time application A k are schedulable, A k is schedulable, or A k is unschedulable. So the schedulability of real-time application becomes the schedulability of its tasks.
Assumption 1: All the tasks are independent and preemptive and the relative deadline of a periodic realtime task is equal to its period.
Assumption 2: The execution time and relative deadline of every real-time task is known after its application is submitted. The execution time of nonreal-time tasks is unknown.
All theorems and statements in this paper are based on these assumptions.

The task is schedulable in the server CUS EDF with size .

div.head: Schedulability Condition of Soft Real-time Task with SD Algorithm
div.p: Most of the SD scheduling algorithms are based on General Processor Sharing (GPS) [9][10][11][12]. GPS is based on the concept of the reservation ratio of processor computation time. In our architecture, we use a constant utilization server [4,5] to execute the soft real-time tasks with SD algorithm. Suppose a GPS server executes at a rate (which is less than or equal to one), and each task t i has a reservation ratio u i which is a positive real number. Each task t i is guaranteed to be served at a rate of g i = ∑ j j i u u independent of the actual workloads of other tasks. In other words, the guaranteed CPU service rate g i for task•t i will not be affected by the actual behavior of any task t j , i ≠ j. The enforcement of the guaranteed CPU service rate for a task must rely on an admission control mechanism to manage the total workload of a system [13].

The GPS-based scheduling allows any ready task to use any left-over CPU time in the system. Therefore, the system will not be left idle as long as there are tasks waiting to be executed. On the other hand, with the guaranteed CPU service rate, a real-time task can meet all its deadlines as long as its actual workload does not exceed its reserved rate, i.e. u i ≤ g i .

div.head: Performance Evaluation
div.p: One common criterion to evaluate the performance of a real-time scheduling framework is to measure the overhead used by the scheduler. When comparing two different scheduler implementations, we usually compare the time used to make scheduling decisions.

For real-time systems, another important performance criterion is the task response time which includes interrupt delay, context switch time, scheduling delay and others. Different implementations of the same scheduling algorithm may have different scheduling delays. The scheduling delay in our hybrid scheduling scheme is the time from the occurrence of a scheduling chance to before the context switch for this scheduling point.

Another important performance criterion is the deadline missing rate, which is defined as the ratio of the number of the real-time task instances having missed their deadlines to the number of all real-time task instances. Each sporadic task is a task instance. Each period of a periodic task is a task instance.

For the purpose of comparison with our hybrid scheduling scheme, we also implement a scheduler based on pure RM and a scheduler based on pure EDF. We carry three experiments (using one of the three schemes respectively) in our real-time system with single Pentium-IV 2G processor and 256MB RAM under Linux 2.4.20.

In these experiments, we use 100 independent and preemptive hard real-time periodic tasks. In the experiment evaluating the hybrid scheme, half of the tasks use EDF algorithm, and the other half use RM algorithm. The execution time of each task is known a priori. The deadline of periodic task is the same as the end of its period.

The three experiments use the same way to submit these tasks, and the interval between the time to submit a task and the time when its previous/next task is submitted is a second. In all experiments presented in this section, data points are collected during the second after one task is submitted. Additionally, the schedulability process is removed in the three experiments.

Fig. 3 shows the variance of average scheduling latency with the number of the tasks running in the system. The result indicates that the scheduler with the hybrid scheduling scheme has lower overheads than EDF and higher overheads than RM under the same environment and workload. 4 shows the variance of deadline missing rate with the number of the tasks running in the system. From Fig. 4, we can see that under the same environment and workload, the deadline missing rate of the real-time systems with pure RM scheduling scheme is higher than the other two schemes, and the lowest is pure EDF scheme. On the whole, the performance of the hybrid scheduling scheme presented in this paper is higher than the pure EDF and RM schemes. Additionally, the hybrid scheme is suitable for jointly scheduling hard, soft and non-real-time tasks in open real-time systems while the other two schemes can not. To get steady testing data, we only use periodic hard real-time tasks in the experiments. Periodic and sporadic hard realtime tasks may coexist in the practical systems. EDF algorithm is the most suitable algorithm to execute sporadic hard tasks, and RM algorithm is the most suitable algorithm for periodic hard tasks. So, if we use EDF and RM to execute sporadic hard tasks and periodic hard tasks respectively in the practical systems, the performance will be improved a little.

Further, for many embedded systems, the flexibility and the reconfigurability of the kernel are more important than its scheduling overheads. The hybrid scheme can be used to implement different real time systems with different goals (such as hard, soft or hybrid real-time systems) and can provide the real-time services with different QoS to the different task modes by adjusting every constant utilization server's size. For example, if we increase the size of the constant utilization server with hard real-time scheduling policy and decrease the size of the constant utilization server with soft real-time scheduling policy, the hard real-time power of the system will be improved, in reverse, the soft real-time power of the system will be improved. The hybrid scheme also simplifies the schedulability analysis and validates the schedulability of the tasks with one scheduling policy independently of the tasks with other scheduling policies.

div.head: Conclusions
div.p: In this paper, a hybrid scheduling scheme for hard, soft and non-real-time tasks is proposed. This scheme uses the basic architecture of the two-level hierarchical scheduling scheme but enhances it very much. When the system with our hybrid scheduling scheme starts, it creates a constant utilization server for each real-time scheduling policy and a total bandwidth server for all the non-real-time tasks with time sharing scheduling policy. The bottom-level scheduler is the operating system scheduler, responsible for maintaining and scheduling all the servers.

The hybrid scheduling scheme can accommodate a much broader spectrum of real-time applications than the two-level hierarchical scheduling schemes. For example, the two-level hierarchical scheduling schemes are not suitable for either the application that consists of real-time part and non-real-time part, or the application with parallel threads or processes in parallel /distributed real-time systems, but our hybrid scheme is able to.

The experimental results show that the hybrid scheduling scheme has higher synthetically performance than pure EDF and pure RM scheme. Further, the hybrid scheme is suitable for jointly scheduling hard, soft and non-real-time tasks in open real-time systems, but pure EDF and RM schemes cannot. The hybrid scheme also has high flexibility and reconfigurability, which can be used to implement different real time systems with different goals (such as hard, soft or hybrid real-time systems) and can provide the real-time services with different QoS to the different task modes by adjusting every constant utilization server's size and also simplifies the schedulability analysis. But the CPU utilization control to the servers is not flexible enough in our scheme. In the future work, we will study the adaptive CPU utilization control to improve the hybrid scheduling scheme.

figure.figDesc: In recent years, the domain of real-time computing has broadened from primarily hard real-time closed embedded systems such as avionics and automotive applications to new open environments with other types of performance constraints such as the Internet and mobile computing systems. The real-time systems in such open environments are called open real-time systems. The most important characteristic of open real-time systems is that they are able to process the applications developed and deployed independently. Thus, open real time systems make a new request for task scheduling.
